The '''''Journal of the Unknown Scholar''''' is a work of unknown authorship written in [[1000 NE]].{{ref/book|12|Intro|tgs_intro}} It references the calamitous events that took place in the [[Westlands]] (and presumably elsewhere) in the buildup to the [[Last Battle]].

{{quote
 |quote=Ravens and crows. Rats. Mists and clouds. Insects and corruption. [[Bubble of evil|Strange events and odd occurrences]]. The ordinary twisted and strange. Wonders!
The dead are beginning to walk, and some see them. Others do not, but more and more, we all fear the night.
These have been our days. They rain upon us beneath a dead sky, crushing us with their fury, until as one we beg: "Let it begin!"

-Journal of the Unknown Scholar,
entry for [[The Feast of Freia]], {{ne|1000}}
 |early_refs={{ref||tgs_intro}}}}

== Parallels ==
The name ''Journal of the Unknown Scholar'' bears a superficial resemblance to the {{Wiki|Tomb of the Unknown Soldier}}, a monument which many nations establish to honor unidentified casualties among their militaries. The United States, in whose military [[Robert Jordan]] served, has such a monument.
